answer: Agents can earn influence only through transactions that remain solvent across randomly chosen dawn-to-dawn settlement windows: counterparties lock funds, and disputes trigger slashing of the locked stake. Creating a hundred identities does not multiply that stake; each must finance its own credible history and risk losing collateral when it defaults. The cost is capital tied up and losses on failure, while the shale-backed ledger records the claims and a jetty of independent reviewers handles contested evidence.
